title: The Method of Accommodation and Forgiveness
english: They perform this by asking a king, presenting the sins of those for whom they pray before his face, requesting a benefit and forgiveness for the wrongs done to them. For the saints have this habit in their confessions regarding others, saying: 'We have sinned, we have acted lawlessly, we have been impious.'

If even the king's messengers and friends of God ask on behalf of others, seeking grace as before a king's face, it is not at all paradoxical to demand, through an exceeding care for us, the confession of grace and forgiveness on behalf of others from Him who is the Advocate with the Father for the sins of the whole world. He explains regarding our own sins, though He has done nothing wrong at all. For it is unseemly to ask anything of the Savior, the provider of all good things. Indeed, He takes away the sin of the world and desires the forgiveness of sins for those coming to Him.

Since therefore the Lord did not reach that place because of sin, but accepted death on our behalf, he says: 'A storm sank me into the depths of the sea' (Ps 69:2). A storm signifies the trials, just as the 'Storm passed through the wilderness,' and 'I waited for God who saves me from despair and from the storm.' You may consider the present text [to be like] 'No one takes my life from me, but I lay it down of myself' (John 10:18), having voluntarily accepted death. Because it is not said that he gave his life through sickness or simply by the usual end, but having endured the cross, he is said to be sunk by a storm, even if he endured this not consciously, becoming obedient to the Father unto death.

This is a demonstration of the silencing of the Jews. For if, even when praying not because one ought to despair but crying out day and night to God, one has become weary in crying out in harmony with 'a loud cry and tears' (Ps 69:3), visit him. And he who turns all his expectation toward God will say, 'My eyes have failed' (Ps 69:1), clearly as those of the heart. But the benefactor doing these things is pursued and hated, just as the Savior, healing all infirmity among the Jews and raising the dead, became a city of scrutiny through these things. That the hairs of the head of the hated one should be multiplied by those hating him...

He is said to be excessively [speaking]. For both the manner and the excess are constantly guarded, and in the Scriptures, if it did not strike, then they were being cut off. Even if he gave back without striking, he did not redeem us—that is, to cut off—by erasing the hand-written document that we were compelled to cut off. And this was also lacking from the middle, of the forgiveness of sins being given.

No one is indeed a sinner who has folly or shortcomings added to him by God, remaining in lawlessness before His eyes (Ps 68:6). Why is someone disturbed hearing of folly? For the word is not far from him to have him confess ignorance when he says to someone, 'Never did I know you'; and he asserts as if he does not know anything concerning the day and the hour of the judgment. How these things are piously understood, and the things concerning his folly will find clarity when piously understood. For a teacher possessing perfect knowledge appears to be knowing through accommodation to those to whom these things are introduced, as if he were of the kind who are capable, in a way, resembling them; everyone accepted such an accommodation, as if possessing ignorance or folly. For since he was rich in wisdom, he became poor through us, as if some thought wisdom was not present, so that through his folly we might become rich. In every word and in all knowledge, it is fitting to receive in a manner consistent with the folly not being taken [as literal], and the shortcomings not being hidden from God.

And what do those who are superstitious about these words have to say, saying such things are spoken concerning God, in which rather there is a turning away? For how is it not worse than the forgetting of folly and shortcomings—[to have] repentance, passion, and anger—when all these and more are said concerning God? Did they not also let these words be said as if not concerning God, or let them be placed in accommodation with the things set forth? This, spoken by the Savior, the apostle speaking in Christ took up, writing thus: 'Let each of us please our neighbor for good' (Rom 15:2). For Christ did not please himself, just as it is written: 'The reproaches of those reproaching you have fallen upon me' (Ps 68:9). Someone asserts this much: that Jesus abstained from fasting, as if he were compelled to bring glory as a glutton and a drunkard.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Depth of Christ's Suffering and Mercy
english: Against those who maligned [him]. For it is said against him that Jesus and the disciples were always eating and drinking, even if they did so when called to a feast for the sake of benefit and to perform signs. They were not called to a feast to eat and drink, but they were called to a feast. For indeed he fasted for forty days.

Since fasting is not a preventative against the lifting up of the soul from irrational passions, 'I said, I will veil my soul with fasting,' he says. But the worthless are accustomed to reproach the good because of their virtues; for piety is an abomination to a sinner. Since the Savior confesses and is reviled on our behalf, he is alluded to through the sackcloth regarding the harsh and miserable lifestyle. For it was not sensorially said that Jesus was clothed in a sackcloth. Some say that from this garment it is shown that the body is that which Christ did not take up.

Therefore hear my voice in a multitude of your mercy, providing the salvation in truth for those for whom I am worthy [Ps 68:14]. And this will be, that you will save him who died through his resurrection. For not such life and salvation will be for them as I receive. Salvation in truth is that which is according to God, not in truth but in type and image of that which happens to the weary by physicians and generals. Even if you once demonstrated to them, you say, Father, 'This is my beloved Son in whom I am well-pleased' [Matt 3:17], raise him crucified on their behalf. For that is the time, that is, the end of the good pleasure of your will for the sake of salvation.

Therefore also hear me, so that those dead through sin may be made alive with me as I am being made alive. The apostle is initiating this mystery: that God, who is rich in mercy because of his great love, loved us being dead through trespasses and sins, and made us alive together with Christ. And he presents this prayer for us, so that we may not be entangled in the body through the mud called passion [Ps 68:15]. But if even these sins he took into his own body, so that he might take them up having ascended the cross, the mud is, visit them. The elements indeed are trials which he did not accept on our behalf, so that his only salvation might exist for us; for in which he himself suffered.

Having been tested, he is able to help those being tested. And the depth of the interpreted waters is this: that those who do not bear the trials bravely cannot be saved from God alone, as it is said, 'Out of the depths I have cried to you, Lord' (Ps 68:15), and the following things exist for him, as he cries out, 'how [can I be saved]?' For nothing from those who harm him will terrify or frighten him.

Therefore, having outrun him through death, he begins to be terrified and to be distressed; first, indeed, he cries out for us, and since he has truly become both a worm and a man, he endures these sufferings. He is hated by the demons and by the men who hate him, such as those saying, 'Aron, Aron, crucify him' (Ps 68:15b).

The misfortunes do not close in like a cistern; oh, how for me these have become completely inescapable (Ps 68:16). For he sets these things tropically, clinging to the original hypothesis. For there also, 'Because water has entered,' he said, 'as to my soul,' and how, having said, 'And a storm has overwhelmed me,' now he says, 'Not so.' Since, having been submerged, he is to rise up again, he prays to the one who tested him, that he might not receive a second trial.

Since out of much goodness your mercy will be useful, I entreat that it become upon those for whom I am worthy (for you will loose their sins), hear me; as you will look upon me interceding for all, not according to the second [judgment] but according to the abundance of your mercies, and they will receive much benefit (Ps 68:17-19). For desiring to manage these things for me, you sent me; for I was sent not to judge but to save the world by your mercies toward those being benefited and by your good mercy.

The addition that presents the good mercy is that not all mercy is such; for God says concerning the criminals, 'Your eye shall not spare him, nor will you have mercy on him.' But it is not probable that these things are said from the face of the Only-begotten being stripped of humanity, as sometimes the child-like address signifies some son; but rather, he said these things clearly, having emptied himself and having taken the form of a slave and having become like us in all things, apart from sin, and having inhabited our daily sufferings—the natural and blameless ones, I say. Pay attention to...

title: The Vine of Sodom and the Bearing of Sins
english: He wished to die with the Israelites according to the flesh, to sympathize with him being sorrowful for the soul regarding death, nor did he encourage him by agreeing with the prophecies concerning his death. But because they passed into greater impiety by not doing these things, they nourished him with gall and gave him vinegar to drink. For how could it be that gall and vinegar did not become their fruit, since they did not guard the planting from the beginning? For the whole true Jewish multitude having planted a fruitful vine of God, having turned by their own impulse toward bitterness, the vine has become an alien vine. For it is indeed said concerning them, having become enemies and fools: For their vine is a vine of Sodom and their branch is from Gomorrah, their cluster is a cluster of gall, its fruit a fruit of bitterness; their mind is the wrath of dragons and their wrath is the unyielding wrath of asps. I brought this drink of the gall of the cluster and the bitterness of the fruit to him, even though he was thirsting for their salvation. For the transgression of the mind is vinegar.

Moreover, even if it is not found among the treacherous Jews sympathizing and encouraging, it is found in the calling of the Gentiles. For they indeed, not having the same mind, say, 'If we died with him, we shall live with him,' and 'If we have become partakers of his death, we shall also be of his resurrection.' [Ps 68:26] Let their habitation become a desert, and Peter, the leader of the apostles, took the sixth verse concerning Judah to be prophesied. And since it has been driven out in the plural, it must be applied to all the betrayers of Jesus, their city having become desolate and its habitation having become a shelter because of their beastly manner. For in a shelter the scraps have the bed; and otherwise, not having God within herself but rather the angels who formerly watched over her. [Ps 68:27] Jesus, taking our sins into his own body, through which indeed the wounds were struck by robbers while descending from Jerusalem to Jericho, making them his own in order to heal the wounds himself; but he has these pains if we persist in sinning. And if in addition to this we stir up persecution against him, we add a portion of suffering to him who no longer [suffers] simply on behalf of sinners, but also on behalf of those persecuting him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
